prompt:
Image 1 is the target art style. Image 2 is a strip of the scroll 清明上河图 (Along the River During the Qingming Festival) and the only source for what this panel shows. Paint one very wide panel of a painted backdrop in exactly image 1's painting style (hand-inked dark-brown outlines, light hatching, flat muted painted colours, clean readable shapes), showing what image 2 paints, but as a view seen at eye level by a person standing on the ground at the edge of our scene and looking out: looking west along the north bank of the canal from the edge of the countryside: the canal's wharves, the next stretch of the scroll (image 2), seen from its east end at eye level. Image 2's right end is nearest to us and its left end farthest away; its top edge is on our right and its bottom edge on our left. All of it is far off across a stretch of white mist, so even its nearest shed, boats and people are small, the people's heads on the horizon. On the left of the picture the river runs away from us to the horizon: a flat, narrow band of blue-green water drawn with long flowing ink current lines and small curling crests, no deeper than a standing man is tall, never a wide sheet of water reaching toward the bottom of the picture; on its far side there is no bank, only white mist. Moored one behind another along the river's right-hand bank, their bows pointing away from us: nearest, a small plain planked boat with a big rudder; then a broad, deep-laden grain boat with a woven-mat hood over its bow and heavy coiled cables piled on its after deck, a ladder leaning down from it to the small boat; then a second big grain boat with two overlapping woven-mat roofs over a small deckhouse at its bow, its cargo under nets of crossing ropes, a high stern gallery and a big rudder, a cleated gangplank running up the bank from its stern; farther on, a big timber boat with a gable-roofed fore cabin, a long flat-roofed plank cabin with a ladder against its side and round bundles along its roof, and a barrel-vaulted mat hood aft; farthest, a big river boat with a broad dark arched mat canopy over its foredeck and a long rounded mat cabin roof heaped with casks and bundles. No mast is up and there are no sails. On the right, the bare earth of the wharf rises gently from the boats to a row of open sheds. Nearest on the right: a long open eating shed under a big hipped thatched roof, with a lower thatched skirt roof along its front, standing on many plain posts over tables and benches with seated customers; at its near end a round-faced man in a light robe sits on a stool holding the lead rope of a small dark donkey. Just behind it stands the fire-watch tower: a platform of horizontal brick courses, about as high as a house's eaves, with a straight wooden stair and hand-rail climbing its side, carrying a small open pavilion of four posts under a pyramidal tiled roof with wide flaring eaves and a round finial; nobody is in it. A few bare willows and bare trees stand behind the shed. On the open wharf in front of the sheds: porters bent under big grain sacks carried up from the boats, a heap of sacks with a stout man seated on it keeping count, two men shaking hands. Farther along on the right: a long open shed under a tiled roof with a hatched mat curtain hanging from its eave and tables beneath it; a house with a small balustraded loft under its gable; a lower open eating shed with a front gable and a flat awning, and a cord of small pennants running from its roof to the top of two tall poles leaning together into an A. Behind them, a tall open frame of long poles and two leaning ladders stands free in an empty yard, and at the far right, along the top of the bank, a long single-storey shop open along its whole front, its shelves stacked with paper goods, a tall narrow signboard on a post at its end. Then, on the bank beside the river, a huge old pollard willow with a thick, twisted, knotted trunk leaning out over the water to a massive knobbed head; a raised plank walkway with a slatted railing runs along the bank beside it, and behind it a big open eating shed with a huge tiled roof, a flat woven-mat awning on posts over its tables and a big round mat parasol. Farthest, where the bank meets the horizon: a white-walled house with a hipped tiled roof, a closed warehouse with tall lattice doors on a plank-faced platform, and a long riverside hall with a row of big open windows under one huge tiled roof, an open shop with a big dark curtain drawn up at one end beside it; along the far right edge, a back street of small tiled sheds on posts with tables, a round-topped cart and a horse with its head down. The willows are pollard willows before their leaves open: from each knobbly head a half-open fan of long, straight, stiff bare shoots springs upward and outward. They are NOT weeping willows: no hanging curtains, no drooping strands, no foliage. Leave out the huge dark willow with a burled trunk that fills image 2's bottom right corner: it stands on our side of the edge and is not part of this view; there only the small boat and the water show. No stone quay or embankment, no bridge, no city wall, no gate tower, no pagoda, no second tower, no hills, no lake, no island, no far shore, no sails, no banners other than the small pennants.

Rules for the panel:
- Only what image 2 paints. Add nothing that image 2 does not show: no hills or mountains, no distant tree lines or forests, no lakes, rivers or islands, no towers, pagodas, city walls, flags, clouds, birds, sun or haze banks, unless the description above names them. Leave out image 2's red seals, inscriptions and silk damage.
- Eye level. The viewer's eye is at the height of a standing person's eyes, so the horizon is one straight, level line across the whole image, a quarter of the way up from the bottom edge. The heads of all standing people are on that line, near or far; buildings, trees, carts and animals rise above it with their feet just under it. Below the horizon there is only a thin strip of level ground, a tenth of the image height at most. We never look down onto roofs, courtyards or the surface of a road: a road running away from us is a thin wedge of ground narrowing to the horizon.
- Plain white everywhere else. The sky is flat pure white from the top edge down to the horizon, behind everything: no clouds, no blue, no gradient, no haze, no texture, no paper grain. Below the strip of ground the bottom of the image is the same pure white: the ground ends in soft white mist. The upper part of the image, above the tallest trees and roofs, is empty white.
- Clear and crisp: every outline and colour as clear as in image 1, with no atmospheric haze and no fading toward the distance (the world adds its own mist). Trees keep clear branches and twigs with white showing between them.
- The left and right eighths of the image hold only low ground and a few small things; they will fade into mist.
- Colours of the real town in soft spring daylight, as in image 1: grey-blue clay tiles, white lime plaster, weathered brown timber, tan rammed earth and dusty roads, pale fresh-green willows, dark green pines, bare ink-brown branches. Not the yellow-brown of the aged silk in image 2; no paper texture, no border, no frame, no seal, no text, no signature.
